cim: Trump pushes to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' in bid to reshape tech narrative
cim_eredeti: Trump pushes to rebrand AI as 'super intelligence' in bid to reshape tech narrative
szoveg_eredeti:
by KRISTINE FRAZAO | The National News Desk

WASHINGTON (TNND) — President Donald Trump is pushing to replace the term “artificial intelligence” in government language, arguing the widely used label is inaccurate and should be scrapped in favor of what he calls “super” intelligence.

The president posted online that he wants to officially ban the terms “AI” and “artificial intelligence” in all relevant documents and other materials “due to its inaccuracy.” (TNND)

“We're leading everybody with what they called artificial intelligence. But I said it's not artificial. It's, it's really super,” Trump said during an October 14 rally.

The president posted online that he wants to officially ban the terms “AI” and “artificial intelligence” in all relevant documents and other materials “due to its inaccuracy.” The move follows an Executive Order Trump signed last month making a similar declaration for official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports and policy documents.

In an interview with The National News Desk on Wednesday, Aalok Mehta, Director of the Wadhwani AI Center at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, responded.

He said it may not have the intended effect. “In a lot of ways, superintelligence is an even more sort of science fiction sounding word, right? It it it go. It's even farther down the spectrum of things humans have invented that perhaps we can't control,” Mehta said.

The debate comes as some communities have raised concerns about the data centers that power some AI systems, and as leaders in the industry continue to warn about potential risks.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman described the stakes in stark terms while speaking at the Stanford Graduate School of Business last week:

Altman added, “I no longer think were going to be able to patch all the bugs think we're going to have to completely switch the defense model to sort of using the same technology for sort of a new kind of defense shield.”

While Trump can direct terminology used in federal communications, he does not have the legal authority to ban people or companies from using the term “artificial intelligence.”

Observers are now watching how extensively the administration replaces the terms in official government documents—an effort that could ironically require the use of AI tools to help carry it out.
